content.text: The zone's temperature rose +2.02 °C after July 2018 while other zones rose 0.2–0.8 °C — that's an anomalous step. But the catalog for this building contains only zone air-temperature sensors and their heating/cooling setpoints. There are no occupancy, electric-power, lighting, or CO2 time-series in the store, and no redundant per-room temperature stream to cross-check against. Without those, the data cannot tell whether the extra heat is a real load increase or a drift/fault of the single zone sensor.
